title: 33 pre-existing tests/integration failures on origin/main (10 files) — failing and leaking, independent of GH #439
symptom: With BPM_TEST_DB_URL pointing at a healthy running test database, `zig build test-integration` reports 33 failing test blocks across 10 already-wired integration test files. The failures split into two kinds: outright assertion/query failures (reported as `error: '<file>.test.<name>' failed:`) and memory leaks (reported as `leaked N allocations:`). tests/integration/iss202_merge_atomicity_test.zig alone accounts for 8 leaking blocks (TC-ISS-202-03/04/05/06/07/10/INT-01/INT-03).
root_cause:
Six distinct causes across the ten files, plus one umbrella-level blocker that had to be cleared first.

BLOCKER (found first): tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig - wired into main_test.zig by THIS run's own commit baea783 (GH #439) - did not compile (29 errors). The test-integration umbrella therefore aborted at the configure phase and never ran a single binary, which is why the original triage saw only 31 failures: it was measuring an aborted run, not the suite.

REAL PRODUCTION BUGS (3):
1. src/engine/instance.zig freeOwnedTransitionState() hand-rolled the TransitionResult teardown and diverged from the canonical version beside the allocation. It called ObjectMap.deinit() (frees only the bucket storage) on state.variables/join_counters, which transition() builds with cloneObjectMapSafe - every key dupe and every heap-backed value leaked, one allocation per variable, on EVERY create()/advance(). It also freed each EmittedEvent's idempotency_key but never its payload, leaking a TIMER's duration_iso8601/repeat_expression/payload_json, a SERVICE_TASK's spec_json/correlation_key, a sub-process's child_definition_id. Fixed by delegating to transition_mod.freeTransitionResult (made pub). This single fix cleared the entire iss202 leak cluster (all 10 blocks) plus leaks in ee09, instance_error, ee01, ee08, ext01.
2. src/engine/transition.zig PARALLEL_GATEWAY split branch never freed the token that ARRIVED at the gateway (filtered out of new_tokens and replaced by per-edge tokens) nor the superseded state.tokens outer array - 4 allocations leaked per parallel split. The JOIN branch beside it already did this correctly. Six unit-test fixtures that passed stack arrays of string literals had to be converted to dupeTokenSlice to satisfy the ISS-0601 allocator-owned contract the fix now enforces.
3. migrations/GBL-125/126/127 (EXP-301/302 effects) are GBL-prefixed, so the runner applies them to public ONLY - but each is guarded by to_regclass(<prereq>) IS NULL THEN RETURN and every prereq (instance_projections, event_type_registry, tasks) lives exclusively in per-tenant schemas after GBL-073. The guard was always NULL in public, the bodies never ran, and all three were recorded as applied. effects_outbox HAS NEVER EXISTED in any schema. This is the GH #335 / ISS-0076 anti-pattern recurring across three files at once. Fixed by migrations/1136_iss0149_exp301_effects_outbox_tenant_scope.sql (plain-numeric, so it runs per-schema; the same guards now do their intended job).

TEST BUGS (3):
4. iss106_webhook_outbox_test.zig 'Rejected value #2' inserted 'PENDING' (uppercase) while its own comment said 'legacy lowercase pending'. Migration 085 migrates values UP to uppercase and the live CHECK accepts 'PENDING' - the test asserted the exact opposite of the contract it verifies. Corrected the literal to 'pending'.
5. sch303_timer_dlq_test.zig used a hardcoded idempotency key literal (timer-fired:<fixed-uuid>) while timer_id was a per-test random UUID. scheduler.zig builds the key as timer-fired:{timer_id}, so the pre-inserted collision row could never collide - the fire always SUCCEEDED and the retry-exhaustion path the test exists to exercise never ran. Derived the key from timer_id (3 sites).
6. audit_chain_utf8_test.zig: TestHarness.init() sets session_replication_role='replica' session-wide (so resetTestData can DELETE audit_entries past the immutability guard), which suppresses ALL user triggers - including trg_bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash, the exact trigger every test in the file exercises. Rows landed with chain_hash NULL and the assertions read that NULL as a broken hash. Scoped a session_replication_role='origin' override around the two insert paths (TC-03 also surfaced once TC-01/04 stopped passing vacuously on NULLs).
reproduction:
1. Ensure docker-compose db_test is up and healthy and BPM_TEST_DB_URL is set.
2. git checkout origin/main
3. zig build test-integration
4. Observe 33 `error: '<file>.test.<name>' failed:` / `leaked N allocations:` lines across the 10 files listed in affected_areas.
impact: test-integration is not green on main, so it cannot function as a release gate: a real regression introduced into any of these 10 areas would be indistinguishable from the existing noise. The 8 leaking blocks in iss202_merge_atomicity_test.zig are the most concerning subset — a leak in merge/transaction code is a plausible production defect rather than a test-fixture artefact, and merits triage before the assertion failures.
candidate_resolution: Triage per file rather than as one batch; the ten files span unrelated subsystems (audit chain, task claim, webhook outbox, merge atomicity, idempotency keys, error retry, task guard, timer DLQ) and almost certainly have distinct causes. Suggested order: (1) the iss202 leaks, since a leak is either a real ownership bug in merge code or a fixture that fails to free — both worth knowing; (2) audit_chain_utf8 / audit_iss103, which share the audit chain trigger and may have a single common cause; (3) the remainder individually. Note GH #366 (test-integration-others-internal barrier deadlocks, 40P01) and GH #359 (tenant_default shadow table) are open against this same suite and may explain a subset — check those before diagnosing from scratch.
notes: Discovered while wiring 21 previously-unwired integration test files into tests/integration/main_test.zig under ISS-0137 / GH #439. Once those files compiled, running the suite surfaced this pre-existing failing set alongside them. Filed separately rather than fixed inline per the WF-03 handoff constraint: this is a genuinely distinct defect set from the wiring defect, it is not a regression of the wiring change, and diagnosing 10 unrelated subsystems is far outside the scope of a build-graph fix. GH #439's own acceptance criteria (lint_test_wiring.py exit 0, zig build exit 0, zig build test exit 0) are all met independently of this issue — the Green-Main Gate covers `zig build test`, which is service-free and green; this issue is confined to `test-integration`.
resolution:
All ten files named in GH #465 now pass DETERMINISTICALLY IN ISOLATION - verified across 2 consecutive clean runs each of test-integration-{iss0122,iss103,iss102,iss106,iss202,iss203,iss205,iss207,iss208,sch303}, zero failures. iss202_merge_atomicity_test, the priority subset, went from 10 leaking blocks to 0.

Full-suite totals fell from 253 failing blocks to 167. zig build, zig build test, python tools/lint_test_wiring.py, python tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests and python tools/lint_test_isolation.py tests/integration all exit 0.

NOT GREEN: zig build test-integration still exits 1. Two documented reasons, neither in this issue's scope:
(a) GH #366 / ISS-0107 cross-binary contention. Under the ~20-way concurrent umbrella, 15 files intermittently fail with 55P03 lock timeouts in TestHarness.init->runMigrations, and with fixture-stomping signatures (ItemNotFound, HTTP 404 where 409 expected, 'expected 1 found 0', 23505 on uq_event_idempotency) caused by sibling binaries' resetTestData() TRUNCATEs. EVIDENCE that this is contention and not a defect in these files: every one of them passes 2/2 isolated runs, and the same block passes or fails depending only on which siblings are scheduled alongside it. GH #366 is open against exactly this mechanism.
(b) tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig: 14 of its 30 blocks still fail - filed as ISS-0158 / GH #479. That cluster needs a production-behaviour decision about whether transition() should emit effect_emitted on SERVICE_TASK entry (it currently emits nothing, so TC-EXP-302-02/03/04/06/07/08 panic on emitted_events[0]).
prevention:
1. Never keep a second copy of a teardown routine in a different module from the allocation it mirrors. Both leaks in src/engine/ were exactly this: instance.zig maintained its own freeOwnedTransitionState while transition.zig already had freeInstanceState/freeTransitionResult next to cloneObjectMapSafe. Export and delegate; a duplicate teardown drifts silently the moment the allocation side gains a field.
2. A migration whose DDL targets a per-tenant table MUST NOT carry the GBL- prefix. The to_regclass guard makes the mistake invisible: the body no-ops and the ledger records success. When adding a GBL- migration, verify its guarded prerequisite actually exists in public - three consecutive files (GBL-125/126/127) got this wrong and the omission survived because nothing ever queried the tables.
3. When a test file's entire subject is a database trigger, check what the harness does to session_replication_role before trusting any assertion about trigger output. A suppressed trigger yields NULL, and a NULL read as 'wrong value' looks like a hashing bug rather than a trigger that never fired.
4. A test that pre-seeds a collision row must derive the colliding value from the SAME source production uses. sch303 hardcoded the key while production derived it from a random per-test UUID, so the collision the test's whole premise depends on never happened - and the test passed by exercising the success path it was written to rule out.
5. A test literal that contradicts the comment directly above it is a defect, not a style issue (iss106's 'PENDING' under a 'legacy lowercase pending' comment). Check assertions against the migration they verify.
6. A configure-phase compile error in ANY member of an aggregated test step makes the whole step's failure count meaningless. ISS-0149 was originally scoped from a 31-failure run that had actually aborted before executing anything; the true surface was ~250. Confirm the suite RAN before triaging its results.
